Independent integer Gaussian/incidence evaluations reproduce the polynomial F_r for 24 (q,n) instances q=2,3,4,5 and n=6..11; sample q=2,n=6 gives (18880,448,-64,64). The proof, not these finite checks, controls all q,n: factorizations of N(1),N(q),N(q^2),N(q^3) have strict signs at admissible parity and P(z),L(z) are positive increasing for z>=q^4. Fourier inversion and alternating-rank multiplicities give the exact absolute kernel norm and no-zero invertibility.

value.rationale: Determining the sign pattern of a natural rank-at-most-four ball over every finite field, no-zero Fourier boundary and exact endpoint norm is a meaningful global structural result that is not supplied by mere character eigenvalue listings.

final_claim: For every prime power q>=2 and n>=6, the alternating rank<=4 ball has no zero Fourier coefficients and precisely one negative dual rank orbit r=floor(n/2)-1; all coefficients have an explicit quadratic formula in q^(n-2r) and the sharp l1/linfty Fourier projection norm is an exact orbit-weighted expression.
limitations: Only rank<=4 balls of alternating forms n>=6, exact counting-measure Fourier projection; no rank>=6 classification, no claim of certified exhaustive priority.
